Jeff Caldwell goes unclaimed on waivers and reverts to Kansas City Chiefs' injured reserve; here's what can happen next | A to Z Sports

The first option to discuss is the injured-reserve stash. Caldwell can choose to stay on injured reserve for the entire 2026 NFL season. It will effectively be a redshirt season for him, where he can get healthy and turn his attention to 2027. This is usually the best option for long-term development, but it can also delay the inevitable. That happened last season with UDFA LB Brandon George . The Chiefs released George before 2026 OTAs even began. The second option is to agree to an injury settlement and join another team once he's healthy. The Chiefs have five days to offer Caldwell an injury settlement. They have to pay him for the games he'll miss with his knee hyperextension. Then they would release him from injured reserve. At that point, he'd be allowed to sign with 31 other NFL teams, but would be unable to sign to the 53-man roster in Kansas City.

articles.title: Micah Parsons calls out Bo Nix and Drake Maye over NFL Top 100 ranking of Jordan Love
articles.summary: The NFL Top 100 list is finally drawing to a close, with the league’s top 10 players now in the process of being revealed. Naturally, there is a lot of conve...
articles.body:
The NFL Top 100 list is finally drawing to a close, with the league's top 10 players now in the process of being revealed.

Naturally, there is a lot of conversation over some of the rankings, with 92 of the Top 100 now named.

Green Bay Packers defender Micah Parsons is no stranger to voicing his thoughts on what is right and wrong in the NFL.

The Top 100 list has proven no different, with the 27-year-old now venting his frustrations over the ranking of his quarterback, Jordan Love .

Bearing in mind that the Packers missed out on the playoffs last season, Love was ranked 72nd, which was four spots lower than he managed the year prior.

As the list narrows down on the best player in the NFL, Parsons has called out some of the quarterbacks to rank higher than Love.

Micah Parsons calls out Bo Nix over NFL Top 100 ranking

Since Love replaced Aaron Rodgers as the starting quarterback in Green Bay , the Packers have been unable to make it past the Divisional Round.

Last season's 9-7-1 record eventually saw the Packers eliminated in the Wild Card Round for the second consecutive year, yet Parsons feels Love should be ranked higher.

"See, no, no, no. I'm pretty sure Bo Nix had more interceptions, and they probably were tied around the same passing touchdowns," said Parsons .

The Denver Broncos quarterback was not the only to receive backlash from Parsons over his ranking, though, with Detroit Lions QB Jared Goff also feeling the heat.

"They had Jared Goff rated higher than Jordan Love. We swept the Detroit Lions last year, and Jordan Love put up 30-plus on one of the top defenses in the NFL. Like, come on, bro," Parsons added.

The irony is that although Love's quarterback rating has increased year on year, the number of touchdowns he has thrown has actually decreased in each of the last three seasons.

Even Super Bowl runner-up Drake Maye could not escape Parsons' wrath, with the Packers defender debating how much better of a season Maye actually had than Love,

"That's because he went to the Super Bowl. He had an amazing year, second MVP, but I don't know if he's 50-plus slots better than he's not."

To say Parsons is clutching at straws is an understatement. For his QB to rank higher than he did this year, Love needs to put more than nine wins on the board and progress deep into the postseason.

Until then, he won't be considered as one of the top guys in the league.

articles.title: C.J. Uzomah holds an interesting stat in Bengals history
articles.summary: From one franchise QB to the next
articles.body:
The Bengals brought back a familiar face this week in C.J. Uzomah to officially retire from the game of football in Cincinnati.

Uzomah was a big-time fan favorite in the Queen City before leaving after the 2021 season to sign with the New York Jets .

During his time as a Bengal, Uzomah had many memorable plays, but he also holds quite an interesting stat that no one else has.

The former Cincinnati tight end caught Andy Dalton 's final touchdown pass as a Bengal and the first touchdown pass thrown by Joe Burrow .

The Dalton-to-Uzomah score occurred in the first quarter during a 33-23 victory over the Cleveland Browns on December 29, 2019. The Burrow-to-Uzomah score occurred during a 35-30 loss to the Browns on September 17, 2020.

So not only did he catch both touchdown passes, he caught both touchdown passes against the same division rival. You just can't make this up.

Uzomah was a big piece of the Bengals' success in 2021, and it is cool to see him back in town talking to guys like Burrow and others during practice.

He will also be the 'Ruler of the Jungle' during the Bengals ' Week 4 matchup with the Jacksonville Jaguars .

articles.title: Texas A&M junior WR named to USA TODAY's Top 100 CFB player rankings
articles.summary: Texas A&M WR Mario Craver was the only Aggie named to USA TODAY's Top 100 college football player rankings ahead of the 2026 season.
articles.body:
It's fair to say that Texas A&M enters the 2026 season under the radar, no matter how much talent third-year coach Mike Elko has returned and acquired from the transfer portal months after leading the Aggies to the College Football Playoff for the first time in program history . However, after a record 10 players were selected in the 2026 NFL Draft, the national perception is that the Aggies will take a step back this fall.

Until the games are played, predictions are meaningless, but they do provide a window into what fans should expect, and with the new nine-game SEC schedule, half of the conference could end the season at 9-3 or 8-4, making the College Football Playoff Committee's job that much harder, knowing that a 9-3 team has yet to make the 12-team field.

Texas A&M 's brutal schedule includes road tests vs. LSU , Missouri , Alabama , South Carolina , and Oklahoma before hosting the Texas Longhorns to end the regular season. On paper, A&M can afford to lose only two of those games while staying undefeated at home, which would mean defeating Texas for the first time in more than a decade.

On both sides of the ball, Texas A&M's roster is chalk full of NFL talent, while redshirt junior quarterback Marcel Reed returns for his second full starting season, aided by one of the deepest wide receiver rotations in the country, junior Mario Craver , who reeled in 59 receptions for 917 yards and 4 touchdowns after transferring from Mississippi State , was the only Aggie named in USA TODAY's Top 100 college football player rankings.

Coming in at No. 95, writer Austin Curtwright detailed why the elite playmaker made the cut:

"Craver caught 59 passes for 917 yards with four touchdowns last season as a sophomore, but now has the opportunity to be Marcel Reed 's top target after KC Concepcion was drafted in the first round. The former Mississippi State transfer stalled out late in the season but was on pace for a monster campaign through nonconference play, combining for 443 receiving yards and four touchdowns in Texas A&M's three wins to open the season against UTSA, Utah State and Notre Dame. The explosive 5-9 receiver could be in for a huge year with the Aggies, especially if Reed takes a step forward as a passer."

articles.title: Washington Redskins gear is available to fans in the Commanders' team shop at stadium and online
articles.summary: The Washington Commanders are selling throwback jerseys and T-shirts bearing the Redskins name the franchise discarded in 2020 as racist or offensive.
articles.body: The Washington Redskins name and iconic logo that the NFL team in the nation's capital abandoned in 2020 is back in a manner of speaking. It's on full display and for sale in the team's current merchandise shop. Although the gear bearing the Redskins name is rare and limited to a Mitchell & Ness throwback line of T-shirts or jerseys bearing the name of former players who played with the Redskins name and helmet insignia, it is indeed for sale. Anyone can go to the brick-and-mortar store at Northwest Stadium or online and buy, for example, an Art Monk T-shirt bearing the Pro Football Hall Fame receiver's likeness in his old uniform and in his Redskins helmet. TAYLOR HEINICKE RETIRES FROM THE NFL WITH A FAREWELL SALUTE TO THE WASHINGTON REDSKINS The back of that T-shirt is emblazoned with "Washington Redskins" and Monk's career statistics and records. The shirt costs $49.99. For the same price, fans can purchase a Sean Taylor T-Shirt with the likeness of the former safety in his Redskins uniform before he was tragically slain in 2007. Like Monk, Taylor played for the Redskins, not the Washington Commanders. Taylor's retired No. 21 jersey, complete with the Redskins name on the front and a 75th anniversary Washington Redskins patch, is available for $114.99. The interesting thing about this is the franchise is marketing this gear emblazoned with Washington Redskins script and logos as Commanders gear. The jersey, for example, is described as a Sean Taylor Black Washington Commanders Retired Player Name & Number Mesh Top – even though the Commanders nickname does not appear on the jersey. NFL AND CONGRESS DISCUSS RETURN OF THE WASHINGTON REDSKINS LOGO This is what happens when an NFL franchise builds a long and storied history as the Washington Redskins from 1937 to 2019, then decides the Redskins nickname is racist or otherwise offensive under pressure from liberal fans, some Native American groups and sponsors. The Washington Commanders, as they're known now, have vowed never to return to the Redskins nickname. Current owner Josh Harris said in September 2023 that he understands the nostalgia for the former name but that "there was a portion of our fan base that felt disrespected by the former name." So why, if the Redskins name is bothersome, are the Commanders selling Redskins merchandise? And why are they later this season wearing an alternate helmet with a spear piercing the W insignia, much like the old feathered arrow helmet the Redskins wore in the 1960s? The spear that is part of the so-called "Raise Hail" alternate uniform is an obvious reach at Redskins nostalgia. The gear in the team gift shop is being made available to keep the old trademark in commercial use, according to WUSA9 in Washington. "We are required to maintain the marks in commercial usage so that marks remain under franchise control," a club spokesman told the television station. CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE A trademark may be deemed abandoned if its use is discontinued with intent not resume use. The Lanham Act says that three consecutive years of nonuse is prima facie evidence of abandonment. The statutory standard also requires "bona fide use … in the ordinary course of trade," rather than merely token sales made solely to reserve rights. That might be a problem for the Commanders because their contention is that these Redskins items are sold on a limited availability. It should be noted that there are Native American groups who believe the Redskins nickname to be indeed racist. But other native individuals, including a Navajo Code Talkers Association leader and a former Blackfeet tribal chairman, have publicly supported retaining the old nickname and the Native-profile logo. Walter "Blackie" Wetzel, a former chairman of the Blackfeet Tribe and former president of the National Congress of American Indians, helped persuade the club in 1972 to replace its "R" helmet logo with the Native chief helmet portrait most associated with the team. In a 2002 interview, Wetzel said: "It made us all so proud to have an Indian on a big-time team. It’s only a small group of radicals who oppose those names. Indians are proud of Indians." articles.title: Rams' Sean McVay reacts to wild college football controversy: 'Feel like I took a freakin' gummy'
articles.summary: Sean McVay said he "can't even comprehend" the college football eligibility chaos as SEC and Big Ten block former NFL players from returning.
articles.body: Los Angeles Rams head coach Sean McVay has one way to view the current college football landscape. Tight end Dae’Quan Wright was expected to become the first-ever player to go from an NFL roster back to an NCAA roster on Wednesday. Wright, who was waived by the Cleveland Browns just two days ago, was reportedly set to reunite with his old Ole Miss coach, Lane Kiffin, at LSU for this upcoming college season. But hours after he cleared waivers, Wright and the rest of the college football world saw the SEC and Big Ten, which will soon be joined by the ACC and Big 12, create new guidelines for eligibility that would prevent players like Wright who have participated in professional sports from reentering college athletics. CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE This came after Wright and other players were granted injunctions or temporary restraining orders allowing them to play this upcoming college season. And most of the lawsuits stem from the NCAA’s new guidelines, which give players five years to play five seasons. McVay was asked about the college controversy on Tuesday during his press session at training camp. He didn’t even hear the full question, but his reaction said it all. "Yeah, I can’t even comprehend this stuff," McVay explained. "It’s wild. I don’t know enough about it other than the fact that guys that can be in NFL camps, if it doesn’t go down for them, they can go back college." McVay put it even more bluntly. "I feel like I took a freakin’ gummy," McVay said, per the Los Angeles Times. COLLEGE ATHLETICS' LATEST MESS: COURT ORDERS SAY ATHLETES CAN PLAY, BUT SEC AND BIG TEN READY TO FIGHT Under the new policies set by the SEC and Big Ten, any athlete that has signed with a pro team in the NFL, declared for the NFL Draft or participated in any type of professional training camp will be ineligible for conference competition. Attorney Ryan Downton, who represents a number of players trying to get back into the college landscape, told OutKick’s Trey Wallace on Tuesday night that they are currently "working on a legal strategy" on how to move forward against both the NCAA and the respective conferences that enacted the new guidelines. "The SEC’s actions put the NCAA in contempt of multiple court orders," Downton told OutKick-Fox News on Tuesday night. "It is cartel-like conduct when NCAA conferences attempt to create their own spur of the moment rules in response to Courts enjoining those same rules at the NCAA level." CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Wright is among a group of former college football players who were all granted a temporary restraining order by a judge in Louisiana. He is among several athletes from the 2022 high school class that tried capitalizing on the NCAA’s five-year eligibility guidelines, which was unanimously approved by the NCAA Division I Cabinet in June. OutKick’s Trey Wallace contributed to this report.
